name: St Mark's biofeedback trial
question: In patients with fecal incontinence, do sphincter exercise instruction or biofeedback improve outcomes beyond standard advice?

arms.label: hospital biofeedback plus home electromyogram biofeedback

verdictNote: Exercises and biofeedback showed no advantage over advice; all groups improved.
takeaway: Among 171 patients with fecal incontinence, hospital pressure biofeedback, hospital plus home electromyogram biofeedback, sphincter exercise instruction, and standard advice were compared. Patient-rated improvement was 53% with hospital biofeedback versus 54% with advice; no added benefit was found for exercise or biofeedback.

reports.label: Randomized report
reports.citation: Norton C, Chelvanayagam S, Wilson-Barnett J, et al. Randomized controlled trial of biofeedback for fecal incontinence. *Gastroenterology.* 2003;125(5):1320-1329. doi:10.1016/j.gastro.2003.09.039
reports.followUp: At treatment completion; improvements largely maintained 1 year after treatment

results.note: The abstract highlights this comparison but does not identify a prespecified primary endpoint, denominator, or statistical threshold.

results.measure: Pooled median episodes per week before and after treatment
results.note: In the pooled analysis of available diaries, median accidents decreased from 2 to 0 per week (P < 0.001); 39% of post-treatment diaries were missing, and group-specific before-and-after changes were not given.

results.measure: Pooled median continence score before and after treatment; worst score 20
results.note: In the pooled before-and-after analysis, the median score decreased from 15 to 13 (P < 0.001); Table 3 also reports post-treatment scores by group.

values.home: Hospital biofeedback plus a home electromyogram biofeedback device
